research.provider: Anthropic (Claude API) — direct first-party API at api.anthropic.com
research.auth: Detect by API key prefix `sk-ant-` (full form `sk-ant-apiXX-...`; admin keys use `sk-ant-admin...`). Authentication is via the `x-api-key: <key>` request header (NOT Authorization: Bearer). Every request also REQUIRES the `anthropic-version` header (current pinned value `2023-06-01`). content-type: application/json for POST. Optional `anthropic-beta` header for beta features. This `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` pair is the unambiguous fingerprint distinguishing Anthropic from OpenAI (which uses Authorization: Bearer sk-...) and Gemini (which uses ?key= or x-goog-api-key).

endpoints.purpose: List ALL available models for this key (enumerate, then probe each). More recently released models listed first. Paginate with after_id until has_more=false.
endpoints.notes: Returns {data:[{id, type:'model', display_name, created_at(RFC3339), max_input_tokens, max_tokens, capabilities{...}}], first_id, has_more, last_id}. limit default 20, range 1-1000. Use the returned id strings as the model field when probing. This endpoint also reveals models a custom/enterprise key may have early access to. Cheap (no token cost). 200=ok, 401=bad key. Cursor params: before_id, after_id.

endpoints.purpose: Get one model's metadata (capabilities, max_tokens, max_input_tokens) without inference cost
endpoints.notes: 404 not_found_error if model id unknown / not entitled. Use to confirm a model exists before a paid probe.

endpoints.purpose: CHEAP probe per model to read the anthropic-ratelimit-* RESPONSE HEADERS (the live limits for that model = RPM/ITPM/OTPM). Send with max_tokens:1 and a 1-char input to minimize cost.
endpoints.notes: Required headers: x-api-key, anthropic-version: 2023-06-01, content-type: application/json. Even max_tokens:1 yields a 200 with FULL rate-limit headers. Read headers from a 200 OR from a 429. Probe each model id separately since limits are per-model-family. Opus limit is shared across all Opus 4.x; Sonnet limit shared across Sonnet 4.x. Costs ~a few input tokens + 1 output token. DO NOT use max_tokens:0 (that only warms cache, no generation). Cheapest model to probe is claude-haiku-4-5.

endpoints.purpose: Read configured org/workspace rate limits PROGRAMMATICALLY without making an inference call (alternative to header-probing)
endpoints.body_example: (no body) headers: x-api-key + anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 (Rate Limits API; may require admin key sk-ant-admin)
endpoints.notes: Documented as the Rate Limits API (/docs/en/manage-claude/rate-limits-api). Returns the configured limits per model. If 403/401 with a non-admin key, fall back to the messages header-probe above. Verify exact path against docs as Admin API endpoints live under /v1/organizations/.

endpoints.purpose: Detect org vs workspace structure / list workspaces (Admin API — only works for admin keys sk-ant-admin)
endpoints.notes: 401/403 with a normal sk-ant-api key -> the key is a standard (non-admin) project/workspace key. 200 -> admin key, can read org metadata. Useful to distinguish key class.

research.rate_limit_behavior: A true rate limit returns HTTP 429 with JSON body {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"..."},"request_id":"req_..."} and a `retry-after` header giving the number of SECONDS to wait (earlier retries are guaranteed to fail). The 429 message describes WHICH limit was exceeded (requests vs input-tokens vs output-tokens). Mapping of headers to dimensions: anthropic-ratelimit-requests-* = RPM (requests per minute); anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-* = ITPM (input tokens per minute); anthropic-ratelimit-output-tokens-* = OTPM (output tokens per minute); anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-* = a COMBINED/most-restrictive view (shows the tightest currently-binding limit; if workspace limits don't apply it returns total = input+output remaining). The `*-reset` headers are RFC 3339 timestamps (token-bucket continuous replenishment, not fixed-window). Token-remaining values are rounded to the nearest thousand. NOTE: There is NO documented per-day (TPD/daily-tokens) rate-limit header on Anthropic — daily/monthly control is the SPEND limit (dollars), not a token-rate header. Distinguish from 529 `overloaded_error` (Anthropic capacity saturated, NOT your limit — retry with backoff, no retry-after guarantee) and from "acceleration limits" which also surface as 429 when an org ramps usage too sharply.
research.tier_detection:
Match the key's observed `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-limit` (RPM), `anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-limit` (ITPM) and `anthropic-ratelimit-output-tokens-limit` (OTPM) PER MODEL against the official standard-tier table (values current as of 2026, verified on platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits):

RPM is uniform across model families within a tier: T1=50, T2=1000, T3=2000, T4=4000.

Claude Sonnet 4.x (ITPM / OTPM): T1=30,000 / 8,000 | T2=450,000 / 90,000 | T3=800,000 / 160,000 | T4=2,000,000 / 400,000.
Claude Haiku 4.5 (ITPM / OTPM): T1=50,000 / 10,000 | T2=450,000 / 90,000 | T3=1,000,000 / 200,000 | T4=4,000,000 / 800,000.
Claude Opus 4.x (ITPM / OTPM): T1=500,000 / 80,000 | T2=2,000,000 / 200,000 | T3=5,000,000 / 400,000 | T4=10,000,000 / 800,000.
(Claude Haiku 3.5 retired except Bedrock/Vertex; its ITPM counts cache_read tokens — '†'.)

DETECTION ALGORITHM: (1) probe each model id, read RPM+ITPM+OTPM limit headers; (2) find the tier whose triple exactly matches for the relevant family; (3) the easiest discriminator is RPM (4 distinct values 50/1000/2000/4000) combined with ITPM to disambiguate; (4) if all three match a column -> assign T1..T4. The spend tiers correspond to cumulative credit-purchase thresholds: T1=$5 (max purchase $500, monthly spend cap $500), T2=$40 ($500/$500), T3=$200 ($1,000/$1,000), T4=$400 (max purchase $200,000, monthly cap $200,000). Org advances tiers automatically on reaching the credit-purchase threshold (note: Claude Platform on AWS does NOT auto-advance — starts at Tier 1, increases via account rep).
research.extra: ENTERPRISE / CUSTOM (企业级) DETECTION LOGIC: If a key's observed limit headers do NOT exactly match ANY standard T1-T4 column for the model family, mark it 企业级 (enterprise/custom). Concrete signals: (a) RPM not in {50,1000,2000,4000}, or RPM=4000 but ITPM/OTPM EXCEEDS the T4 ceiling (e.g. Sonnet ITPM > 2,000,000, Opus ITPM > 10,000,000, OTPM > 800,000) — only enterprise/Monthly-Invoicing or a negotiated custom limit produces above-T4 numbers; (b) limit values that fall BETWEEN documented tier columns (non-standard negotiated number); (c) presence of `anthropic-priority-*-tokens-*` headers with non-zero limits indicates a Priority Tier (committed-spend) plan = enterprise-class; (d) Monthly Invoicing accounts have NO monthly spend cap (vs T4's $200,000) — not header-visible but pairs with above-T4 rate limits. ORG vs PERSONAL / KEY CLASS: project/workspace keys (`sk-ant-api...`) can call /v1/messages and /v1/models but get 401/403 on /v1/organizations/* Admin endpoints; admin keys (`sk-ant-admin...`) succeed on Admin API (/v1/organizations/workspaces, members, etc.). Workspace-scoped keys may show LOWER limits than the org (workspace sub-limits) — the anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-* header surfaces the most-restrictive (workspace) value, so a key under a constrained workspace can look like a lower tier than the org actually is; cross-check requests-limit + input-tokens-limit together. RECOMMENDED classification: exact T1-T4 match -> that tier; above-T4 or non-standard or priority-headers-present -> 企业级 (enterprise/custom); below-standard on one limiter only -> workspace-throttled (note it).
research.model_names: Chat/text (NO image generation — Anthropic does not offer any image-generation model; all models are text-output, with text+image+PDF INPUT/vision only). Current (June 2026) flagship/default: claude-opus-4-8 (most capable). Latest per family: Opus = claude-opus-4-8; Sonnet = claude-sonnet-4-6 (best speed/intelligence, good cheap probe with thinking); Haiku = claude-haiku-4-5 (alias) / claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (fastest + CHEAPEST to probe at $1/MTok in, $5/MTok out). Legacy/still-available: claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-5(-20251101), claude-opus-4-1(-20250805), claude-sonnet-4-5(-20250929). Deprecated (retire 2026-06-15): claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-opus-4-20250514. Always treat model IDs as CONFIGURABLE — enumerate live via GET /v1/models rather than hardcoding, since the list changes and a key may have custom early-access models. Model IDs from the 4.6 generation onward are dateless but still pinned snapshots; earlier aliases (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5) resolve to a dated snapshot.
research.gotchas: DISTINGUISHING ERROR CLASSES (critical for a probe to not misclassify): 401 authentication_error = bad/revoked/missing key (key itself invalid). 402 billing_error = billing/payment problem (this is the dedicated 'no credits / billing disabled' signal — check Console payment details). 403 permission_error = valid key but lacks permission for that resource/model (e.g. not entitled to a model, or non-admin key hitting Admin API). 404 not_found_error = unknown model id (invalid/misspelled/unavailable model on POST or GET /v1/models/{id}). 400 invalid_request_error = malformed body (bad params, also catch-all for other 4xx); a wrong model NAME on /v1/messages typically returns 404 not_found_error, while a structurally invalid request returns 400. 429 rate_limit_error = a TRUE rate limit (has retry-after seconds). 413 request_too_large (Messages API >32MB, returned by Cloudflare before reaching API). 500 api_error / 504 timeout_error = internal/timeout. 529 overloaded_error = Anthropic-wide capacity saturation, NOT your quota — do not treat as rate limit. ERROR SHAPE is always JSON: {\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"<error_type_string>\",\"message\":\"...\"},\"request_id\":\"req_...\"} and a `request-id` response header on every response. TO KEEP PROBING CHEAP & SAFE: use max_tokens:1 with a 1-char prompt on the cheapest model (claude-haiku-4-5); read headers from the 200 response (no need to trigger a 429). Avoid max_tokens:0 (cache-warm only, no generation, still bills cache tokens). Note cache_read_input_tokens do NOT count toward ITPM for current models (only Haiku 3.5 '†' counts them), so a probe with no cache is fine. To map limits per model you MUST probe each model id separately (limits are per-family, Opus 4.x shares one bucket, Sonnet 4.x shares one bucket). Rate limits are currently shared across inference_geo values (us/global draw the same pool). HIGH-RATE PROBING WARNING: rapid back-to-back probes can themselves trip 429 (token-bucket bursts) or 'acceleration limits' — space probes out (1/sec is safe at T1's 50 RPM) and ramp gradually; a 429 during probing is meaningful (it reveals the limit) but back off per retry-after. Headers expose ONLY rate limits (RPM/ITPM/OTPM), never the dollar spend limit or remaining credit balance — those are Console/billing-only.

research.provider: Google Gemini / Generative Language API (ai.google.dev, host generativelanguage.googleapis.com)
research.auth:
Two interchangeable schemes, both accepted by generativelanguage.googleapis.com:
1) HEADER (current recommended): `x-goog-api-key: <KEY>` plus `Content-Type: application/json`. This is what all 2026 docs/quickstarts show.
2) QUERY PARAM (legacy, still works): append `?key=<KEY>` to the URL. Older docs/SDK examples use this; useful as a fallback probe.

KEY DETECTION (this is how to recognize a Gemini/Google key by pattern, NOT documented on the api-key page but well-established): keys are 39 chars total, case-sensitive prefix `AIza`, followed by 35 chars from [A-Za-z0-9_-].
  - Broad Google regex: `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}`
  - Narrower Gemini/AI-Studio variant observed: `AIzaSy[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{33}` (prefix `AIzaSy`, still 39 total).
The `AIza` prefix is just a routing identifier, not a security/validity signal — format match != active key. Confirm liveness with a real call (HTTP 200). OAuth bearer tokens are an alternative auth path but those are not `AIza...` keys.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/auth probe + cheapest text generation (validate key, classify tier by 429 timing). Use a Flash model for cheapest probe; Pro model when caller wants a 'pro' check.
endpoints.url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{MODEL}:generateContent  (MODEL configurable, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash for cheap probe, gemini-2.5-pro / gemini-3.1-pro-preview for 'pro'). Header: x-goog-api-key: <KEY>  OR  ?key=<KEY>. Use v1beta for newest models; v1 is stable subset.
endpoints.notes: maxOutputTokens:1 minimizes output token cost; thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel:low (or thinkingBudget:0 on 2.5 models) avoids paying for hidden reasoning tokens. For pure auth/rate-limit probing, a 1-token prompt is the cheapest possible billable call. Endpoint is the same for every model — only {MODEL} and version (v1/v1beta) change, so keep both fully configurable.

endpoints.purpose: Image-generation probe (detect whether key/tier can hit an image 'flash-image' model and observe its separate quota bucket).
endpoints.url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{IMAGE_MODEL}:generateContent  (IMAGE_MODEL configurable, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash-image, gemini-3.1-flash-image, or imagen line). Auth identical to text.
endpoints.notes: Image models bill per generated image and have their OWN per-model quota (a 429 here references a different model dimension than the text model). Minimal prompt keeps cost low but image generation is far more expensive than a 1-token text call — fire sparingly. Some examples use responseModalities ["TEXT","IMAGE"]; ["IMAGE"] alone is accepted. All outputs carry a SynthID watermark. Imagen uses a :predict endpoint variant rather than :generateContent — verify per model.

endpoints.purpose: List models available to THIS key (cheap GET, no generation cost) — useful to enumerate what tier/key can access and to validate the key without spending generation quota.
endpoints.url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models  (auth via x-goog-api-key header or ?key=). Append ?pageSize=1 to keep response tiny.
endpoints.notes: Returns 200 + model list if key is valid; returns 400/403 with API_KEY_INVALID/PERMISSION_DENIED if not. Does NOT consume generate_content quota, so it's the safest first liveness check before any rate-limit probing. Also reveals which model IDs exist (avoids guessing).

rate_limit_headers: NONE — the Gemini / Generative Language API does NOT expose rate-limit/quota in response headers. There is no X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After, or quota header on success responses. Remaining/limit quota is only viewable in Google AI Studio (Rate Limits tab), not via API headers. The ONLY machine-readable limit info is inside the 429 JSON body's details[] (google.rpc.RetryInfo.retryDelay, google.rpc.QuotaFailure.violations[].quotaValue/quotaId). Probe must therefore infer limits empirically from 429 timing, not from headers.
research.rate_limit_behavior:
HTTP 429 with canonical status "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED". Body shape:
{"error":{"code":429,"message":"You exceeded your current quota... https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits","status":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED","details":[
  {"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.QuotaFailure","violations":[{"quotaMetric":"generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests","quotaId":"GenerateRequestsPerMinutePerProjectPerModel-FreeTier","quotaDimensions":{"location":"global","model":"gemini-2.5-pro"},"quotaValue":"..."}]},
  {"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.Help","links":[{"description":"Learn more about Gemini API quotas","url":"https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits"}]},
  {"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.RetryInfo","retryDelay":"34s"}
]}}

Key parsing notes for precise 429 timing while firing ~50 req/s for 30s:
- There is NO standard `Retry-After` HTTP header. Backoff hint lives ONLY in details[] where @type == google.rpc.RetryInfo, field `retryDelay` formatted as a duration string like "13s" / "34s" / "52s" (sometimes longer). Parse the trailing "s".
- `quotaId` discriminates WHICH limit you hit: ...PerMinute... (RPM, short retryDelay seconds), ...PerDay... (RPD, long delay / lockout till midnight Pacific), and token variants GenerateContentInputTokensPerModelPerMinute/Day. `quotaValue` is the numeric limit that was crossed — capture it; it's the best empirical signal of the actual RPM/RPD/TPM for that key+model+tier.
- `quotaDimensions.model` + the FreeTier/-Tier suffix in quotaId/quotaMetric (e.g. "...FreeTier" vs paid) tells you the tier the limit was charged against.
- Limits are PER PROJECT, not per key; multiple keys/apps in one project share the pool, so 429 onset reflects project-level state.
research.tier_detection:
Two complementary methods:
A) READ THE 429 BODY (authoritative, no extra calls): when a 429 fires, inspect details[].QuotaFailure.violations[].quotaId / quotaMetric. A "-FreeTier" suffix (e.g. GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier, generate_content_free_tier_requests) => Free tier. Absence of FreeTier / paid metric names => a paid tier. `quotaValue` gives the exact crossed limit.
B) EMPIRICAL 429-TIMING CLASSIFICATION (when no 429 yet, or to map Tier1/2/3): fire the controlled burst (~50 rps / 30s) at a fixed {MODEL} and measure how many requests succeed before the first 429 and the returned quotaValue/retryDelay. Compare against documented tier thresholds.

IMPORTANT: Google NO LONGER publishes exact RPM/TPM/RPD per-tier numbers in the static docs (they redirect to AI Studio), and "specified rate limits are not guaranteed." So per-model RPM/TPM thresholds must be treated as configurable/observed, NOT hardcoded. What IS documented are the TIER QUALIFICATION + billing-cap thresholds, usable to map an observed-spend/limit profile to a tier:
  - Free: active project / free trial.
  - Tier 1: linked active billing account; billing cap ~$250.
  - Tier 2: cumulative paid $100 AND 3 days since first successful payment; cap ~$2,000.
  - Tier 3: cumulative paid $1,000 AND 30 days since first payment; cap ~$20,000–$100,000+.
Also documented Batch-enqueued-token limits scale by tier (e.g. gemini-2.5-pro Tier1 5,000,000 vs Tier2 500,000,000) and can corroborate tier. RPD resets at midnight Pacific. Free->Tier1 upgrade is ~instant; later upgrades within ~10 min.
research.extra:
Org/project structure: Gemini Developer API keys are scoped to a Google Cloud PROJECT (not an org/user header like OpenAI's openai-organization). Rate limits and tier are PROJECT-level, applied per project not per key — multiple keys in the same project share quota and tier. There is no per-key tier; tier is a property of the project's linked billing account history.
- List-models endpoint (cheap, no generation cost): GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models (and /v1beta/models/{model} for one). Use this to validate a key and enumerate accessible models without spending quota.
- Paid status is DYNAMIC: a project on a paid tier still returns errors if its Prepay credit balance is $0 (keys in projects linked to a depleted prepay account stop working) — this looks like a quota/permission failure, not a clean 429, so distinguish "out of money" from "rate limited."
- Distinct from Vertex AI Gemini (cloud.google.com / aiplatform), which uses OAuth + project/location path and different quota semantics — detection here is specifically the generativelanguage.googleapis.com + AIza-key path.
research.model_names:
MUST be configurable — Google rotates/deprecates model IDs frequently and 429 quota is per-model. Best-guess current (2026) defaults:
- Pro text: `gemini-2.5-pro` (stable) or `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (preview). (`gemini-3-pro-preview` now deprecated/shutting down.)
- Flash text (cheapest probe): `gemini-3.5-flash` (current stable) or `gemini-2.5-flash`; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` for cheapest-of-all.
- Image ('flash-image'): `gemini-2.5-flash-image` ("Nano Banana"), `gemini-3.1-flash-image` ("Nano Banana 2"), `gemini-3-pro-image` ("Nano Banana Pro"); Imagen line via separate model id (e.g. imagen 4) using a :predict-style endpoint.
Treat all of the above as runtime config with sane defaults; verify against GET /v1beta/models at startup since IDs and stable/preview status drift.
research.gotchas:
- Auth failure vs rate limit vs billing are DIFFERENT codes/strings — do not conflate:
  * Invalid/missing/leaked key => 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT (often message "API_KEY_INVALID") or 403 PERMISSION_DENIED ("API key doesn't have required permissions" / "Your API key was reported as leaked. Please use another API key."). These are NOT 429 — exclude them from rate-limit timing.
  * True rate limit => 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with QuotaFailure+RetryInfo in details[]. THIS is the only signal to count for timing.
  * 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION => "Gemini API free tier is not available in your country" / billing not enabled — a region/billing gate, NOT a rate limit (looks like failure on every request, no retryDelay).
  * Paid project with $0 prepay balance => requests rejected despite a paid tier; treat as billing-disabled, not rate-limited.
  * 503 UNAVAILABLE / 500 INTERNAL / 504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED => server overload/size errors, transient — do NOT classify as quota/tier signal; retry with backoff.
- DETECTING TRUE 429 vs noise: only count responses with HTTP 429 AND status=="RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" AND a details[] QuotaFailure. Reported quirk: sometimes 429s persist even after honoring retryDelay (backend quota-sync lag), so combine retryDelay with exponential backoff + jitter; don't assume retryDelay is exact.
- MAKING PROBES CHEAP: prefer GET /models for liveness (zero generation cost); for generation use Flash + maxOutputTokens:1 + thinkingLevel:low/thinkingBudget:0 + 2-3 char prompt. Avoid image calls except when explicitly probing the image bucket (much pricier).
- HIGH-RATE PROBING (~50 rps/30s) realities: limits are PER PROJECT, so the burst exhausts the shared project pool, not the key; RPM and RPD are separate buckets — you may hit RPM in the first second (short retryDelay) or trip RPD (long delay/lockout till midnight Pacific) which can lock the project for the day. Parse quotaId to tell minute vs day before deciding to keep firing. RPD lockout is a real cost: a daily-limit 429 means further probing that day is futile.
- No rate-limit response headers exist — all empirical timing must come from request success counts + the 429 body, never from headers.

research.auth: Bearer token in `Authorization: Authorization: Bearer sk-...`. Detect OpenAI by key prefix: `sk-proj-` (project key, default since mid-2024, ~165 chars), `sk-svcacct-` (service-account key, also calls models), `sk-admin-` (Admin/management API only, CANNOT call inference models), or legacy bare `sk-` (user-scoped, still works, no longer issued). DISTINGUISH FROM ANTHROPIC: any key starting `sk-ant-` is Anthropic (`sk-ant-api03-` standard ~108 chars passed via `x-api-key`, `sk-ant-oat01-` OAuth/subscription token), NOT OpenAI. Rule: starts `sk-ant-` => Anthropic; any other `sk-...` => OpenAI. Optional scope headers: `OpenAI-Organization: org-xxx` and `OpenAI-Project: proj_xxx` (only needed for legacy user keys belonging to multiple orgs; project/service keys already carry scope and a mismatched org header triggers a 401 "OpenAI-Organization header should match organization for API key").

endpoints.purpose: Cheap chat call to read rate-limit headers (read x-ratelimit-* without spending much)
endpoints.notes: Cheapest probe. Use max_tokens:1 (newer reasoning/GPT-5.x models may require max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens - if you get a 400 unsupported_parameter, retry with max_completion_tokens:1). Every successful response carries x-ratelimit-limit-requests, x-ratelimit-limit-tokens, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens, x-ratelimit-reset-requests, x-ratelimit-reset-tokens, AND openai-organization (org id/slug). Prefer a cheap model like gpt-4o-mini to minimize cost while still reading org-level shared limits.

endpoints.purpose: List models — cheapest auth/validity check (no token spend); read openai-organization header
endpoints.notes: Zero token cost. 200 = key valid. The openai-organization RESPONSE header here returns the org id/slug. Does NOT return x-ratelimit-* limits the way chat does (those are per-model). Good for cheap validity + org-id detection. 401 with error.code invalid_api_key = bad key; 429 with error.code insufficient_quota possible if billing exhausted.

endpoints.purpose: Get organization NAME (not just id) + user info associated with a key
endpoints.notes: BEST way to get org NAME. Returns an object with an `orgs`/`orgs.data` list; each org object has {"object":"organization","id":"org-xxxx","title":"My Org Name", ...}. The `title` field is the human-readable org display name. Works with a normal project/user key as Bearer. There is NO public GET /v1/organizations endpoint that returns the name — use /v1/me. The openai-organization response header only gives the id/slug, not the title.

endpoints.purpose: Image generation — image model probe + IPM 429 surfacing
endpoints.notes: Best-guess current image model ids (KEEP CONFIGURABLE): gpt-image-2 (2026 flagship), gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1, legacy dall-e-3/dall-e-2. Image limits are measured in IPM (images per minute) + RPD, not TPM. Smallest billable call = n:1, size 1024x1024 (gpt-image still costs money per image - there is no truly free image probe; if cost matters, infer image tier from the chat-derived org tier rather than actually generating). A 429 here surfaces identically: HTTP 429 with error.code rate_limit_exceeded (IPM/RPD exceeded) OR error.code insufficient_quota (billing). New/unverified orgs often get instant 429 even with balance because image models require org verification.

endpoints.purpose: Admin/management plane (requires sk-admin key, NOT a model key) - list projects/keys
endpoints.notes: Only works with an sk-admin- key (management plane). Endpoints live under /v1/organization/* (projects, users, invites, admin_api_keys, audit_logs). These return LISTS of sub-resources, NOT a single org-name object - so do NOT rely on these for org name; use /v1/me. A normal sk-proj-/sk-svcacct- key gets 401 here; an sk-admin key gets 401 on inference endpoints.

research.rate_limit_behavior: A true rate-limit returns HTTP 429 with JSON body error.type = "rate_limit_exceeded" and error.code = "rate_limit_exceeded". Message form: "Rate limit reached for <model> in organization org-xxx on tokens per min (TPM). Limit: 500000 / min. Current: 487234 / min." Limits enforced across 4+ independent dimensions: RPM (requests/min), TPM (tokens/min), RPD (requests/day), TPD (tokens/day), plus IPM (images/min) and audio-minutes/min for those model types - hitting ANY one yields 429. The reset headers x-ratelimit-reset-requests / x-ratelimit-reset-tokens are durations like "1s" / "6m0s" (Go-style duration strings, NOT epoch). A Retry-After header (seconds) MAY be present on 429s - honor it. Recommended handling: exponential backoff with jitter; do NOT hammer (failed requests still count toward the per-minute limit). Note limits can be enforced over sub-minute windows (e.g. a 60k/min limit may burst-fail). To detect a TRUE rate-limit vs quota: a 429 with error.code "rate_limit_exceeded" is retryable; a 429 with error.code "insufficient_quota" is billing (NOT retryable).
research.tier_detection: Tiers are spend-based, applied per-ORGANIZATION (not per key), so header limits reflect the org tier. To infer tier: make the cheap chat probe and read x-ratelimit-limit-requests + x-ratelimit-limit-tokens for a known model, then compare against the documented per-model/per-tier table. Qualification thresholds (cumulative all-time spend incl. credits): Free=$0; Tier 1=$5 paid (no wait); Tier 2=$50 cumulative +7 days; Tier 3=$100 +7 days; Tier 4=$250 +14 days; Tier 5=$1,000 +30 days. CONCRETE per-tier limits for a flagship chat model (GPT-5.5, early-2026 docs - keep configurable): Free=not supported / ~3 RPM, 10,000 TPM, 200 RPD; Tier 1=500 RPM, 500,000 TPM; Tier 2=5,000 RPM, 1,000,000 TPM; Tier 3=5,000 RPM, 2,000,000 TPM; Tier 4=10,000 RPM, 4,000,000 TPM; Tier 5=15,000 RPM, 40,000,000 TPM. (Legacy GPT-4o reference: Tier1=500 RPM/30,000 TPM/10,000 RPD; Tier5=10,000 RPM/800,000 TPM.) gpt-image-2 IPM per tier: Free=unsupported (3 RPM/200 RPD), T1=5 img/min, T2=20, T3=50, T4=100, T5=250. Practical matching: compute the model's reported limits and pick the closest tier row; the TPM jump (e.g. 500k=>T1, 1M=>T2, 2M=>T3, 4M=>T4, 40M=>T5 for GPT-5.5) is the most discriminating signal. WARNING: numbers vary by account/model and change frequently - always treat the docs table as configurable defaults and prefer live header values.
research.extra: Org-vs-personal detection: (1) The openai-organization RESPONSE header on EVERY call returns the org id/slug (e.g. org-xxxx) - presence/value tells you which org served the request. (2) For the org NAME (display title), call GET /v1/me and read orgs[].title. (3) Key-type signals org structure: sk-proj- = scoped to one project inside an org (own rate limit/billing line/model list); sk-svcacct- = service account (project-scoped, not tied to a person); legacy bare sk- = user-scoped (billed to org default project, may belong to multiple orgs so may need OpenAI-Organization header). (4) Project keys/service keys already carry their org+project scope, so sending a conflicting OpenAI-Organization header => 401. (5) There is NO public GET /v1/organizations list endpoint for normal keys; management of org resources is via /v1/organization/* with an sk-admin- key only. (6) List-models endpoint = GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models (cheap, zero-token, returns openai-organization header; also a model-discovery source to learn which models a project key can access).

research.gotchas: Three error classes to disambiguate by error.code (NOT by HTTP status alone): (A) HTTP 429 + error.code/type "rate_limit_exceeded" = true rate limit, RETRYABLE with exponential backoff; (B) HTTP 429 + error.code "insufficient_quota" (message "You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details") = BILLING/no-credits, NOT retryable - retrying wastes attempts and still counts toward limits; (C) HTTP 401 + error.code "invalid_api_key" = bad/revoked/wrong key, NOT retryable. So BOTH rate-limit and quota share HTTP 429 - you MUST read error.code to branch. Make calls CHEAP: use GET /v1/models (0 tokens) for validity+org-id; use chat with max_tokens:1 (or max_completion_tokens:1 on GPT-5.x/reasoning models) to read x-ratelimit-* limits; AVOID actually generating images (always costs money - infer image tier from org tier instead). High-rate probing breakers: failed 429s still count toward the per-minute window so back off (honor Retry-After); limits may be enforced over sub-minute bursts; new/unverified orgs get instant 429 on image models even with balance (org verification required); new accounts may need 24-48h activation after first payment; admin keys (sk-admin-) 401 on inference, model keys 401 on /v1/organization/*. Free trial credits were discontinued (early 2024) - a "valid" key with no credits returns insufficient_quota, which looks like a rate limit but is billing.
